about.heading: About
paragraphs: I'm an IT Support Engineer at **Amazon in Austin, Texas**, the **sole IT point of contact for an entire site** — acting team lead for two IT Support II technicians and four equipment coordinators, primary on-call, and the escalation point operations leadership calls first. My world is real infrastructure: **AWS Outposts, the WAN room, Cisco Catalyst switching, Dell PowerEdge servers, domain controllers, DHCP, and IP migrations**.

Before Amazon, I spent two years at **National Seating & Mobility** acting as an internal MSP — branch-to-branch escalated network work, Azure and Microsoft 365 / Entra ID administration, Intune and endpoint management, in a HIPAA-governed healthcare environment. That followed desktop and endpoint roles in Nashville and Accra, Ghana, where I started in 2019.

My reputation is simple: **permanent fixes, not band-aids.** I trace recurring issues to root cause, kill them for good, and write the SOPs so the team resolves them at first touch. Now I'm widening the base — systems administration, networking, cloud, and automation, with security on top — through a foundations-first training program I call **the Dojo**.

bullets: **Sole IT for the entire site** — acting team lead for 2 IT Support II technicians and 4 equipment coordinators, primary on-call, and the point of contact senior operations leadership escalates to.

Run site infrastructure end to end: **AWS Outposts**, the WAN room (AT&T carrier circuits, fiber plant, ISP/vendor coordination), **Cisco Catalyst 9200/9300** core and access switching, Dell towers and PowerEdge servers, and domain controllers.
Delivered an **800+ camera deployment** for the facility; own DHCP reservations, IP migrations, and thin-client provisioning across the site.
Known for **permanent fixes**: trace recurring issues to root cause and write the SOPs the team resolves them with at first touch. Ticketing in ServiceNow and SIMT.
Acted as an **internal MSP** — the branch-to-branch escalation point for network and systems issues across a multi-site healthcare provider.

Administered **Azure** (VM and device admin), **Microsoft 365 and Entra ID** (licensing, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams), with PowerShell / Microsoft Graph and Power Automate / Power Apps in the toolkit.
Endpoint management with **Intune, System Center (SCCM), and Apple Business Manager**; HIPAA-trained, supporting systems under patient-privacy rules.
Front-line IT support — troubleshooting hardware, software, and connectivity issues for end users, with escalations documented and tracked through the ticketing queue.
Desktop support engineering for one of Ghana's largest electronics and IT retailers — diagnosing and repairing systems, supporting users, and keeping machines in service.
Where the career started: three years of hands-on desktop support — builds, break/fix, user support, and the fundamentals everything since is built on.

dojo_loop.title: The Mastery Loop
dojo_loop.text: One loop per project, no shortcuts. The bar doesn't drop — an unfinished loop isn't done.

dojo_tracks.title: Hardware Foundations
dojo_tracks.description: A+ depth without the courseware: components, builds, diagnostics — physical teardowns where possible, virtual builds where not. Project 1 kicks off here.

dojo_tracks.title: Linux & RHEL Administration
dojo_tracks.description: RHEL is the primary distro — the enterprise sysadmin track. Services, storage, users, hardening, troubleshooting from a blank console.

dojo_tracks.title: Networking — Full Chain
dojo_tracks.description: End-to-end scenarios, modem → edge router → core → access → servers. Cisco IOS and SG300 CLI, MDF/IDF reality, not single-device drills.

dojo_tracks.title: AWS + Terraform
dojo_tracks.description: The IaC rule: if it was built in the console, it gets rebuilt in Terraform. No click-only builds — five Terraform projects and an IaC capstone.

dojo_tracks.title: Azure & Hybrid AD
dojo_tracks.description: AZ-104, then AZ-800/801: Windows Server DC + Entra Connect + site-to-site VPN to Azure — the hybrid identity stack enterprises actually run.

dojo_tracks.title: Security & Automation
dojo_tracks.description: Kali-based security work and automation across everything above — scripting the toil away and learning how systems break so I can keep them standing.

dojo_tracks.title: Local AI Inference Lab
dojo_tracks.description: Self-hosted AI on my own iron: RTX 3050 GPU passthrough on Proxmox, a local model served with llama.cpp, and a tok/s dashboard to watch it run like an operator. Talos Kubernetes and GitOps come in a later phase — experience-first, no datacenter GPUs needed.

dojo_empty.text: **Build Log #1 lands here soon.** Passed projects get published as build-log entries — what I built, what broke, what I fixed, in my own words. First up: Project 1, hardware foundations.

path.heading: The Path
path.intro: The 10–15 year plan: every phase makes the next one harder to replace. Support → infrastructure → infrastructure with security. Versatility, built deliberately.

milestones.title: The Lead Title & the Degree
milestones.description: Finish the WGU B.S. in Cloud and Network Engineering (expected Feb 2027) while stepping into a lead-level support role — deeper scope, bigger systems, first architecture conversations. CCNP study begins off the fresh CCNA.

milestones.title: Infrastructure Engineer
milestones.description: The pivot from support to building: Terraform everywhere, Kubernetes fundamentals, and the Azure hybrid path — AZ-104, then AZ-800/801, with AZ-305 and AZ-700 behind them. The RHEL lab becomes the daily driver.

milestones.title: Infrastructure + Security
milestones.description: Layer security on top of the infrastructure base — CISSP once the domain years are in hand. The goal state: an infrastructure engineer who does security, operating in cloud, trusted with the hard incidents.

milestones.title: Principal / Architect
milestones.description: Principal or staff-level engineering, solutions architecture, or technical leadership — the multi-domain story written all the way down: support, systems, networks, cloud, security. Built in the open, one documented project at a time.
